data.title: Choose the correct answer for each question.
data.description: Mixed conditionals, third conditionals, and modal nuance

sections.question: Choose the correct sentence.
sections.summary: Third conditional for unreal past situations.
sections.explain: Third conditional structure: If + past perfect, would have + past participle.

answers.answer: If she had studied harder, she would have passed the exam.
If she would have studied harder, she had passed the exam.
If she studied harder, she would have passed the exam.

sections.question: Choose the correct sentence.
sections.explain: Mixed conditional: If + past perfect, would + base verb (present result).

answers.answer: If I had accepted the offer, I would be working abroad now.
If I accepted the offer, I would have been working abroad now.
If I had accepted the offer, I would have worked abroad now.

sections.question: Choose the correct sentence.
sections.explain: Second conditional uses past simple + would + base verb.

answers.answer: If the company invested more, it would grow faster.
If the company would invest more, it grew faster.
If the company invested more, it would have grown faster.

sections.question: Choose the correct sentence.
sections.summary: Modal perfect for possibility in the past.

answers.answer: She might have missed the meeting due to traffic.
She might missed the meeting due to traffic.
She might has missed the meeting.

sections.question: Choose the correct sentence.
sections.explain: 'Could have' expresses past ability or possibility that did not happen.

answers.answer: They could have solved the problem earlier.
They could solved the problem earlier.
They could have solve the problem earlier.

sections.question: Choose the correct sentence.
sections.explain: Formal inversion removes 'if': Had + subject + past participle.

answers.answer: Had I known about the delay, I would have left earlier.
Had I knew about the delay, I would have left earlier.
Had I known about the delay, I would leave earlier.

sections.question: Choose the correct sentence.
sections.explain: If + past simple (present unreal), would have + past participle (past result).

answers.answer: If he were more organised, he would have finished the project on time.
If he was more organised, he would finish the project on time.
If he had been more organised, he would finish the project on time.
Unless they had acted quickly, the damage would have been worse.
Unless they acted quickly, the damage would have been worse.
Unless they had acted quickly, the damage would be worse.
If she applied, she might get the position.
If she would apply, she might get the position.
If she applied, she might got the position.

sections.question: Choose the correct sentence.
sections.summary: Third conditional for regret and reflection.
sections.explain: Third conditional expresses regret about past events.

answers.answer: If we had planned more carefully, we would not have encountered these problems.
If we planned more carefully, we would not have encountered these problems.
If we had planned more carefully, we would not encounter these problems.
